process_observations.observation: The declared checker's exit-code behaviour matched the plan's own step-note prediction exactly: exit 0 with W1 (no rule active) and two I3 lines (480 = 8h), with no E2 or E7 firing, confirming the builder avoided both fixture-found constraints by construction.

The manifest check is fully consistent on the first pass: one type (EscalationRules), one member (Case), one file, no wildcard and no coverage-gap exclusion needed — the simplest possible shape for this always-on check.

The status transition to tested applied cleanly via build_plan.py while a concurrent runner was writing plan.json for M4-S02; the two steps share no artefact path and both writers used the CLI only, so no conflict occurred.

Carried verbatim from the owning agent's envelope and artefacts/M4-S04/deploy-order.md § 5, not resolved by this test run: notifyCaseOwner true on a Billing-queue-owned case resolves at run time to billing@acme.example, a live Email-to-Case intake address, so a case escalating while owned by the Billing queue notifies into its own intake mailbox. This is a milestone-gate adjudication, not a checker failure — no declared test asserts sender/recipient identity.

deploy-order.md § 3 records five UNVERIFIED items (U1 custom-field criteriaItems spelling, U2 null Case.BusinessHoursId behaviour, U3 email routing to a queue with no <email>, U4 the escalation engine's batching interval, U5 a possible one-active-rule ceiling). None is covered by any declared acceptance test on this step — all five require sandbox verification the tester cannot perform — so they are carried forward as context rather than adjudicated here.

Both manual acceptance tests are now recorded as usable (Given/When/Then shape present, observable outcome named) but neither is ticked; they and the milestone-scoped businessHoursSource/24x7-calendar assertion still need collection into the human checklist.
